theme: Gedaliah the governor; the people ask Jeremiah
readingInstruction: Read Jeremiah 40:1-42:22. After Jerusalem falls, a Babylonian-appointed governor is murdered, and the survivors ask Jeremiah what to do. Read their promise to obey in chapter 42, and notice what happens in chapter 43, which you will read tomorrow.
settingTheScene: After the destruction of 586 BC, Nebuchadnezzar appointed a Jewish governor, Gedaliah, at Mizpah to oversee the people who remained. Jeremiah chose to stay with them. Then a member of the royal family, Ishmael, assassinated Gedaliah and others. The remaining leaders were afraid of Babylonian reprisal and thought of fleeing to Egypt. They came to Jeremiah and asked for God’s guidance.
observation: The captain of the guard says, “The LORD your God pronounced this disaster against this place” (40:2).
Jeremiah chooses to stay: “Jeremiah went to Gedaliah… and lived with him among the people who were left in the land” (40:6).
“But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam would not believe them” (40:16).
“Let the LORD your God show us the way we should go, and the thing that we should do” (42:3).
“Whether it is pleasant or unpleasant, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God” (42:6).
“If you will remain in this land, then I will build you up and not pull you down” (42:10).
“Do not go to Egypt… I solemnly warn you this day that you have gone astray at the cost of your lives” (42:19-20).
interpretation:
The Babylonian captain gives Jeremiah a choice: come to Babylon and be cared for, or stay in the land. Jeremiah stays with the poor. He had been faithful to God’s word in the city, and he stays faithful among the remnant. For a moment, there is hope. Gedaliah, a good man who protects the people, calls them to settle, serve Babylon, and gather the harvest of the land. The people return from the countries where they had fled, and for a short time there is a summer harvest of wine and fruit.

Then Ishmael, who had been warned, murders Gedaliah at a meal. The murder of the governor and the group around him is shocking, and Ishmael kills pilgrims on their way to the temple as well. Johanan rescues the captives, but he fears Babylon’s reaction.

Johanan and the people come to Jeremiah. Their request sounds pious: “Pray for us to the LORD your God… that the LORD your God may show us the way.” They promise to obey, whether it is good or bad. Jeremiah prays, and after ten days, God answers: stay. “Do not fear the king of Babylon.” If they stay, God will build them up. If they go to Egypt, the sword and famine they fear will follow them there.

The problem is in the heart. Jeremiah says, “You have deceived yourselves.” They had already decided to go to Egypt. They asked for God’s word, but they only wanted his approval. Asking for guidance when you have already decided is not seeking God. The promise to obey whatever he says is easy to make before you know the answer. True obedience begins when what God says is unwelcome.
connection: Jesus said in Luke 6:46, “Why do you call me Lord, Lord, and not do what I tell you?” James 1:22-25 warns against hearing without doing. Proverbs 3:5-6 says to trust in the LORD with all your heart and to lean not on your own understanding. Matthew 7:21 says that not everyone who says “Lord, Lord” will enter the kingdom. John 7:17 says that anyone who wills to do God’s will shall know.
application:
Before you ask God for guidance on a decision, tell him honestly that you will obey whatever he says.

Notice whether you have already decided what you will do and are only asking for confirmation.

Be like Jeremiah this week: stay faithful in a hard place with those who have little.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to show you the way you should go.
Tell him you will obey, whether pleasant or unpleasant.
Ask him to keep you from deciding first and asking later.
